prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Dallas. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Dallas for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — but to give accurate, useful names and phone numbers I need one quick detail: are you in Dallas proper (zip code or neighborhood) or somewhere in the Dallas–Fort Worth metro area? Also: do you have dental insurance, prefer a low-cost option, or need an implant type (single tooth, multiple, All‑on‑4, immediate load)? Any medical issues (diabetes, smoking) that matter?

While you reply, here’s a short, practical plan so you know what I’ll look for and why each kind of practice matters:

1) Which specific practices you should call (types, and why)
- Board‑certified oral & maxillofacial surgeons — call for surgical placement, bone grafting/sinus lifts, extractions and complex cases. They handle the surgical side and complications. Good if you need IV sedation or significant bone work.
- Board‑certified periodontists specializing in implants — call for implant placement focused on gum health and long‑term tissue stability. Excellent for aesthetic front‑tooth work or when periodontal disease is present.
- Prosthodontists — call if your restoration is complex (multiple teeth, full‑arch, occlusion issues). They design and place the implant crown/bridge/denture and coordinate with surgeons.
- Implant-focused general dentists (with advanced implant training) — call for straightforward single-tooth implants and coordinated same-office care. Often more convenient and cost‑effective for routine cases.
- Dental school / university clinics (if cost is a concern) — call for lower-cost care from supervised residents; may be slower but high quality.

2) What I will check for each practice (and what you should ask on the phone)
- Board certifications (ABOMS, American Board of Periodontology, American Board of Prosthodontics) and years of implant experience
- How many implants they place per year and examples of the implant systems they use (Nobel, Straumann, Zimmer, etc.)
- Whether they do in‑office CT/CBCT scans for planning
- Whether they give written estimates (surgery + abutment + crown) and financing options
- Warranty/guarantee and who handles complications after placement
- Referrals process (if multiple specialists necessary) and whether they coordinate in‑house
- Ask about sedation options, healing time, and whether bone graft or sinus lift is likely

3) How I can help next
- If you give me your zip code/neighborhood and insurance (if any), I will find 4–6 specific, current practices in Dallas (OMFS, perio, prostho, and an affordable clinic/dental school), with phone numbers, addresses, and a 1–line reason why to call each.

Tell me your zip code/neighborhood and any insurance or treatment preferences and I’ll pull together the targeted list.
